selector.rationale: Pityriasis rosea best explains the pruritic eruption, dusky plaques, and hyperkeratotic plaques with a central collarette of scale, supported by punch biopsies of the chest and thigh.

rejected.label: Alcoholic cirrhosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, it does not directly explain the skin findings.

rejected.label: Porphyria cutanea tarda
rejected.why: The patient's skin findings and laboratory results do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not align with this diagnosis, and the skin findings are more consistent with pityriasis rosea.
